# Agios Ends Tebapivat Development in Sickle Cell Disease After Phase 2

Author(s)Alex Hillenbrand

Fact checked by: Victoria Johnson

### Key Takeaways

  * A 12-week, double-blind phase 2 study randomized 59 patients (2:2:2:1) to tebapivat 2.5, 5.0, 7.5 mg QD or placebo, targeting dose–response characterization.
  * Hemoglobin response rates were 43.8%, 47.1%, and 29.4% with tebapivat versus 33.3% with placebo, showing limited separation and no consistent dose-response.
  * Improvements in hemoglobin and hemolysis biomarkers aligned with the expected red-cell PK activation mechanism, supporting class-level biologic activity in SCD.
  * Discontinuation was driven by inadequate clinical differentiation rather than tolerability, as safety findings were consistent with prior SCD experience.
  * Strategic focus shifts to mitapivat, with an sNDA under FDA Priority Review for SCD and a PDUFA target action date of November 1, 2026.
SHOW MORE

Agios ends tebapivat development in sickle cell disease after phase 2 results show no differentiated benefit.

Topline results from a phase 2 trial of tebapivat in patients aged ≥16 years with sickle cell disease (SCD) showed improvements in hemoglobin and markers of hemolysis but did not demonstrate sufficient differentiation to support continued development of the pyruvate kinase (PK) activator, prompting Agios to discontinue the program.

"These phase 2 data further reinforce PK activation as a clinically validated mechanism in sickle cell disease, with tebapivat demonstrating hematologic activity consistent with this class of medicine," said Sarah Gheuens, MD, PhD, chief medical officer and head of research and development at Agios, in a statement. "However, the results did not establish the level of differentiation we believe is necessary to support continued development."

### Tebapivat Phase 2 at a Glance

  * Population: 59 patients aged ≥16 years with SCD

  * Design: 12-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial

# Agios shares tumble after discontinuing sickle cell disease programme following Phase 2 trial (AGIO)

Fiona Craig

July 21, 2026 1 min read

### Stock drops after development setback

Agios Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:AGIO) shares fell 14% on Tuesday after the company announced it will discontinue development of tebapivat for sickle cell disease following results from a Phase 2 clinical trial.

The biotechnology company concluded that the study did not produce sufficiently differentiated results to justify advancing the programme.

## Phase 2 study falls short of development criteria

The Phase 2 trial enrolled 59 patients aged 16 years and older with sickle cell disease and evaluated tebapivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, over a 12-week treatment period.

The primary endpoint assessed hemoglobin response, defined as an increase of at least 1.0 g/dL in average hemoglobin levels during Weeks 10 through 12 compared with baseline.

Response rates reached 43.8% in the 2.5 mg once-daily group, 47.1% in the 5.0 mg group and 29.4% in the 7.5 mg group, compared with 33.3% for patients receiving placebo.

Although the study showed improvements in hemoglobin levels and markers of hemolysis across all tebapivat dose groups, Agios said the findings did not demonstrate enough differentiation to support continued investment in the programme.

## Safety profile remains consistent

The company stated that the safety and tolerability profile of tebapivat was consistent with previous clinical studies conducted in patients with sickle cell disease.

## Focus shifts to mitapivat

Agios will now continue to prioritise mitapivat, its other pyruvate kinase activator, which remains under FDA Priority Review for the treatment of sickle cell disease.

Earlier this month, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration accepted the company's supplemental New Drug Application seeking accelerated approval for mitapivat. The application has a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of November 1, 2026.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
